capitals.note: The page says only that Yuan established the prefecture 'at former west prefecture'; Goryeo's West Capital (Seogyeong) was Pyongyang, which is the researcher's reading.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page lead gives 'northwest Korean Peninsula between 1269 and 1290', the 60 prefectures and cities, and Jabi Pass as the border 'belonged to Liaoyang ministry'. No area; the infobox is empty. The goryeo dossier's keyframes start the loss in 1270 (goryeo_1260 runs to 1269); the page's 1269 is used here, so 1269 is a one-year overlap.

region.text: Dongnyeong: '60 prefectures and cities in northwest part of Goryeo', cut to the land the goryeo keyframes hold (same outline as the goryeo dossier's 1270 loss)

ledger.note: 1269: Ch'oe T'an's rebels hand the north-west to the Yuan. The page: Ch'oe T'an and others 'rose in rebellion in order to exclude Im Yŏn, Military Leader of Goryeo' and 'surrendered to Yuan dynasty with 60 prefectures and cities in northwest part of Goryeo'; the lead gives 1269-1290. The year of the surrender itself is the lead's, not stated in the sentence. [Reviewer jk-02-x, 2026-10-19: month 10 added: the Dongnyeong page dates Ch'oe T'an's rising and surrender to October 1269.]

1270: the rebels' land becomes a Yuan prefecture. 'In following year, Yuan dynasty established Tonggyŏng prefecture at former west prefecture', with Ch'oe T'an nominated commander by the Liaoyang ministry; the year is inferred from 'following year'.

region.text: Dongnyeong: '60 prefectures and cities in northwest part of Goryeo', cut to the land the goryeo keyframes hold (same outline as the goryeo dossier's 1270 loss)

ledger.note: July 1290: Dongnyeong goes back to Goryeo. 'In July 1290, Tonggyŏng prefecture was abolished and jurisdiction was transferred to Goryeo.' The Goryeo under Mongol rule page has 'Goryeo regained formal control of Dongnyeong in 1290'.

ledger.note: July 1290: the prefecture is abolished. The page adds that the Koryŏsa mentions it again in 1364-1370 and offers two hypotheses, not followed here.

wars.note: The Goryeo under Mongol rule page: the Mongols 'backed the rebellion of another group of Goryeo officials in the northwest' and 'created the Dongnyeong Prefecture'; no exact date.

certainty.note: Jabi Pass is the only edge the page names.

sources.title: Dongnyeong Prefecture
sources.note: 1269 rebellion, 60 prefectures, Liaoyang ministry, July 1290 abolition; spelled Tonggyŏng in the text.

sources.title: Goryeo under Mongol rule
sources.note: Mongols backed the rebellion, created the prefecture; 1290 and 1294; vassal for about 80 years.

notes: Colony (Mongol outpost) on Goryeo's north-west, 21 years. The page's text spells the prefecture 'Tonggyŏng' (the Yuan name 東寧/東京) while its title is Dongnyeong. Overlord: Mongol Empire to 1293 (the Yuan label has no year on the page). The goryeo dossier's 1270 loss and 1290 gain carry the same region; its 1270 start is one year later than this dossier's 1269. Goryeo's own vassalage to the Mongols (1259 on) is the suzerain's to record.
